source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Lewisville DFW2 publishes 12 MW of IT capacity, ranking 12th among the 19 Texas data centers that disclose a figure and holding 2.5 percent of the state's 475 MW.

The more useful number is the one that is missing. Texas has 133 mapped data center sites and only 19 publish any capacity, so the 475 MW state total is a floor assembled from the minority of operators willing to state a figure. This campus spreads 12 MW across 200,000 square feet of technical space, which is ordinary density for enterprise colocation. Its certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942, describe a facility built to host regulated finance, healthcare and government workloads.

For AI specifically, 12 MW is small. At the 40 kW per rack density typical of AI training, that is roughly 300 racks, well short of what a frontier training cluster consumes. The compliance portfolio says nothing about GPU power density or cooling for accelerators. The suitability score of 58 is explicitly incomplete, with announced expansion listed as missing, so the assessment reflects published capacity and operator type only.

What the record does not cover matters as much as what it does. It carries no coordinates and no nearest airport, so it says nothing about siting, transmission access or land constraints. It does not say whether the 12 MW is energized or merely designed, whether CyrusOne intends to expand at Lewisville, or how much grid headroom exists in the Dallas, Fort Worth area. Those are the variables that would decide whether this campus ever becomes an AI site rather than a compliance-oriented colocation facility.
